hoods.name: Civic District & Bras Basah
hoods.when: Weekday late morning for museums (cool inside at midday), then dusk on the Padang and drinks on Purvis St from 6pm
hoods.london: South Kensington meets Whitehall: museum quarter wrapped round civic buildings
hoods.nyc: Museum Mile crossed with the City Hall Park blocks
hoods.worth: Yes. This is where Singapore's best museums are (the Asian Civilisations Museum and the Peranakan Museum especially), it holds the city's top restaurant (Odette), and two of its best cocktail bars share one shophouse on Purvis St. Do it in pieces, not one heroic loop in the heat.
hoods.vibe: White colonial set-pieces on a green: the Padang cricket field, the old Supreme Court and City Hall fused into the National Gallery, St Andrew's Cathedral, Raffles Hotel's arcades. Behind them Fort Canning Hill is a properly shaded park with a much-photographed spiral tree tunnel. Armenian St is the quiet, pretty museum lane (Peranakan Museum, True Blue next door). Chijmes is a former convent turned courtyard restaurant compound, part lovely and part corporate-dinner. North towards Bras Basah it gets scruffier and more interesting: Bras Basah Complex is a 1980s block of second-hand and art bookshops, and Purvis St has old Hainanese coffee shops next to Nutmeg & Clove and Last Word. It is dead on Sunday evenings and at its best on a weekday at golden hour.
avoid: The Singapore Sling at Long Bar: a tourist tax in a theme-park room
Walking Fort Canning at 1pm in the sun; go before 10am or after 5pm
Chijmes's generic bar-restaurants on a Friday office-party night

hoods.name: Robertson Quay & River Valley
hoods.when: Evenings from 6pm; weekend mornings for coffee and a riverside walk
hoods.london: Hammersmith riverside with a slice of Hackney (New Bahru)
hoods.nyc: West Village calm with a DUMBO-ish converted-school creative cluster
hoods.worth: Yes, and it is her closest patch (Outram/Havelock side, a 25-30 minute walk or a short taxi from Kampong Bahru). It is the densest cluster of food that fits her taste in this whole patch: Meta and Lerouy next door to each other on Mohamed Sultan Rd, JAG's vegetable-led French at STPI, Kotuwa's Sri Lankan at New Bahru. Clarke Quay itself is the bit to skip.
hoods.vibe: The Singapore River upstream of the bridges is a residential quay: low-rise warehouses, condos, a shaded promenade with joggers and dog walkers, and riverside tables that feel more Sunday lunch than nightlife. Robertson Quay is the café-and-wine stretch (Toby's Estate, Common Man round the corner on Martin Rd). Mohamed Sultan Rd has restored townhouses now holding two of the city's best counter-style tasting menus. New Bahru on Kim Yam Rd is the old Nan Chiau school converted in 2024 into a lifestyle cluster: Kotuwa, The Coconut Club, Artichoke, Bar Bon Funk, shops and a lot of good-looking people. Downstream, Clarke Quay is neon, clubs and touts: walk through it to get to Boat Quay, don't stop. Zion Riverside at the western end is a proper neighbourhood hawker centre.
avoid: Clarke Quay's riverside chain bars and touted seafood
Riverside Point seafood with tourist pricing
Expecting buzz on a Monday: half the good kitchens are dark early in the week
main: Dinner at Meta, Lerouy or JAG
Kotuwa crab curry at New Bahru
Bar Bon Funk for vinyl and cocktails
Coffee + river walk on a weekend morning
STPI gallery (free)
Char kway teow at Zion Riverside

hoods.name: Marina Bay & Gardens by the Bay
hoods.when: Dusk on a weekday: Supertrees at sunset, Garden Rhapsody at 7.45pm, then the bay
hoods.london: Canary Wharf with Kew's glasshouses stuck on the end
hoods.nyc: Hudson Yards with a botanical garden attached
hoods.worth: Do it once properly, at dusk, and you have done it. The Supertrees light show and the Cloud Forest are genuinely spectacular, and Marina Barrage is a lovely free picnic lawn. The food is almost entirely hotel and casino fine dining: a few are excellent (Labyrinth, Shoukouwa, Cherry Garden), but most of it is exactly the expensive, glossy register she doesn't rate.
hoods.vibe: Built on reclaimed land, it looks it: Marina Bay Sands' three towers and the boat on top, the lotus-shaped ArtScience Museum, the Esplanade's spiky durian domes, and across the bay the Fullerton and the CBD towers. The promenade loop over the Helix and Jubilee bridges is the best free thing, especially after dark. Gardens by the Bay is two cooled domes (Flower Dome, Cloud Forest with its indoor waterfall) and the Supertree Grove, which is free at ground level and lit nightly. Inside MBS it is a luxury mall over a casino: celebrity-chef outposts, canal gondolas, crowds. Most restaurants here sit in hotel lobbies or malls. The cheap-eats option at the Gardens, Satay by the Bay, was reported closed from October 2026.
avoid: Dining at MBS on a celebrity name alone
The paid SkyPark deck when the Lantern or Jaan view comes with a drink or a meal
Satay by the Bay: reported closed from Oct 2026
Midday in the Gardens outside the domes
main: Supertrees at dusk + Garden Rhapsody
Cloud Forest
Bay promenade loop over the Helix Bridge
Marina Barrage lawn at sunset
Esplanade free concerts
Drinks at Lantern or MO Bar

hoods.name: Raffles Place, Boat Quay & Shenton Way
hoods.when: Weekday lunch for the hawker centres; 9pm onwards for the Hongkong St bars; avoid Sundays
hoods.london: The City around Bank and Leadenhall, with a riverside pub row
hoods.worth: Walk through it rather than spend a day here. It is worth going for three things: lunch at Lau Pa Sat or Market Street Hawker Centre, Willow's counter, and the cluster of very good bars on and around Hongkong St (28HKS, Offtrack, Pop City x Pony).
hoods.vibe: Glass towers over a shophouse riverbank. Boat Quay's restored shophouses front the river with touted seafood and pubs: pretty from Cavenagh Bridge, poor to eat at. One street back, Hongkong St and Circular Rd hide the better bars behind unmarked doors. At lunch the CBD is a stampede of lanyards into Lau Pa Sat (the Victorian cast-iron market) and the CapitaSpring hawker centre. On weekday evenings Boon Tat St beside Lau Pa Sat closes to cars and turns into satay smoke. On weekends it empties out.

Lau Pa Sat at 12.30pm on a weekday (queues); go at 11.30am or after 1.45pm

hoods.name: Orchard Road & Tanglin
hoods.when: Botanic Gardens at 7am or 5pm; Orchard itself only for a specific errand, or Emerald Hill for a drink at dusk
hoods.london: Oxford Street into Knightsbridge, with Holland Park (Tanglin) at the end
hoods.worth: Orchard Rd is a 2km air-conditioned mall corridor and not worth a day in itself. The reasons to go are the Botanic Gardens (UNESCO-listed and genuinely great), Emerald Hill's Peranakan terraces, Kinokuniya, and a handful of serious tables (Les Amis, Buona Terra, Loca Niru, Imperial Treasure Fine Teochew). Newton Food Centre at the top of Scotts Rd is the famous hawker stop, but it is touristy.
hoods.vibe: Wide boulevard, shade trees, mall after mall (ION, Paragon, Takashimaya, Tangs), with luxury flagships at street level and food courts in every basement. Look for the pockets: Emerald Hill is a quiet lane of ornate 1900s Peranakan terraces with a strip of old bars at the bottom. Cuppage Plaza is an unglamorous block full of Japanese expat izakayas. Killiney Rd at the River Valley end still has old kopitiams. West past Tanglin Mall it turns leafy, expat and residential, and runs into the Botanic Gardens. The dining is mostly in hotels, which is fine for Cantonese and sushi and less fine for anything relaxed.
avoid: Newton touts and unpriced seafood (agree the price before you order)
main: Botanic Gardens early, plus the Orchid Garden
Emerald Hill walk + drink at No.5

places.d: The best museum in the city: pan-Asian trade, religion and craft in a riverside colonial building. The Tang shipwreck gallery is the one to see.
places.tip: Ticketed. Go late morning, then walk out onto the river at Cavenagh Bridge.

places.d: Small, beautiful museum on Straits Chinese culture in an old school building. It is the best primer for the food you'll eat here.
places.tip: Pair it with lunch at True Blue next door.

places.d: The old Supreme Court and City Hall joined under one canopy. The Southeast Asian collection is strong, and the building is half the point.
places.tip: Ticketed. The rooftop over the Padang is the view. Odette is on the ground floor.

places.d: Shaded hill park with colonial history, spice garden and lawns. One of the few central places that feels cool at 8am.
places.tip: Enter from the Tree Tunnel side early before the photo queue forms.

places.addr: Fort Canning Park, near Dhoby Ghaut entrance
places.d: The spiral look-up shot everyone posts. Worth 2 minutes, not a queue.
places.tip: Before 8.30am or skip.

places.d: The history-of-Singapore museum in a domed 1887 building. Good once, a bit school-trip.
places.tip: Do it on a rainy afternoon.

places.d: Former convent with a gothic chapel and a sunken courtyard of restaurants. The architecture is lovely; most of the bars are office-party generic.
places.tip: Come for Whitegrass or Lei Garden, not the courtyard bars.

places.src: World's 50 Best Hotels 2026 (No. 17, via Time Out SG)
places.d: The 1887 colonial grand hotel. Its arcades and courtyards are worth a stroll; the main lobby is guests-only.
places.tip: Look, then eat at 1887 by André or leave. Skip Long Bar.

places.d: Peanut shells on the floor, a S$30-plus Sling and a queue of tourists. It is famous, but the drinking is not good.
places.tip: Only if a visitor insists. Nutmeg & Clove is a 5-minute walk away.

places.src: Time Out SG; NHB Heritage Business Registry; Indie Bookshop Day Oct 2026
places.d: Design, architecture and art bookshop since 1991, in a gloriously dated 1980s block full of second-hand bookshops.
places.tip: Wander the whole of Bras Basah Complex; registry lists unit #04-15, so check.

places.src: Michelin 3 stars 2026; Asia's 50 Best 2026 No. 19 (Best Restaurant in Singapore); Lesley Liu Asia's Best Sommelier
places.d: Julien Royer's French cooking, the city's benchmark. Polished and ingredient-obsessed, and warmer than its reputation in the newly redone room.
places.tip: Book weeks out; lunch is the cheaper way in. This is the one splurge to make.

places.src: Michelin 2 stars 2026 + Opening of the Year 2026; Robb Report SG
places.d: André Chiang's return to Singapore (opened 31 Mar 2026) reworking Raffles' archival dishes with local produce. It went straight in at two stars. There's real theatre here, but the cooking is earned.
places.tip: Over-18s only; reported from S$198++. A la carte exists if you don't want the full set.

places.addr: Level 70, Swissôtel The Stamford, 2 Stamford Road
places.d: Devon-born Kirk Westaway's modern British cooking 70 floors up. Produce-led English food with the best dining-room view in the city.
places.tip: Lunch for the view in daylight at a lower price.

places.d: French technique on Japanese seasonal produce under the Chijmes dome (Hokkaido scallop with Mont d'Or, Miyazaki wagyu). Refined; quieter than the starrier names.
places.tip: Tasting menus only. A good date option.

places.d: Hong Kong Cantonese institution, starred and unflashy. Weekend dim sum is the move.
places.tip: Book weekend dim sum; dinner gets pricier fast with seafood.

places.d: Peranakan home cooking in a house full of family antiques beside the museum. It feels like someone's grandmother's dining room, and the food matches.
places.tip: Ayam buah keluak (black-nut chicken). Closed Sundays.

places.src: Long-running Violet Oon institution; no 2026 critic review found
places.d: Peranakan classics in a colonial-glam room inside the Gallery. Pretty and reliable, but True Blue cooks with more soul.
places.tip: Dry laksa and kueh pie tee for a post-gallery lunch. Confirm it's still open (only older listings found).

places.d: Hainanese coffee shop going since 1934, with chicken rice, pork chop and chap chye. Uneven by Leslie Tay's account, but the real old Purvis St.
places.tip: Hainanese pork chop and chicken rice before drinks at Nutmeg & Clove. Status not re-verified for 2026.

places.src: Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026 No. 12; Tatler Best 20 Bars 2026
places.d: Modern Singaporean cocktails built on heritage and everyday local flavours. Now the city's second-ranked bar, and buzzy without being a scene.
places.tip: Go 6-7pm before it fills; Last Word is upstairs for round two.

places.d: Minimalist Japanese-style bar above Nutmeg & Clove: quiet, precise classics.
places.tip: Ask for a martini.

places.d: LG Han reworks Singapore hawker and childhood dishes with local produce. This is the tasting menu that actually teaches you the city, with a fun front of house.
places.tip: Do it early in her stay. Book ahead.

places.d: Edomae sushi counter, a handful of seats, fish flown from Japan. Counter dining at its most serious.
places.tip: Lunch omakase is the lower entry price.

places.d: Emmanuel Stroobant's contemporary French on the bay. Accomplished but formal.
places.tip: Only if Odette is full.

places.d: Teochew-Cantonese from Chef Fei in a redone room. One of the strongest Chinese kitchens in the city right now.
places.tip: Dim sum lunch is the cheaper way in.

places.addr: Level 55, Marina Bay Sands Tower 1, 10 Bayfront Avenue
places.src: Michelin 1 star 2026 (new) + Sommelier Award; Time Out SG
places.d: Cantonese with dim sum and a big Chinese-wine list, 55 floors up. Glossier than she likes, but critics rate it.
places.tip: Dim sum lunch for the view.

places.addr: Level 2, The Shoppes at Marina Bay Sands
places.d: Tetsuya Wakuda's Japanese-European tasting counter. Famous for the marinated botan shrimp with uni and caviar. Very expensive.
places.tip: Only as a special-occasion counter seat.

places.addr: B1 Galleria Level, The Shoppes at Marina Bay Sands
places.d: Starred steakhouse inside the casino mall: excellent beef, but this is the celebrity-outpost register she dislikes.
places.tip: Skip unless someone else is paying and wants steak.

places.d: Tempura omakase counter in an unlikely mall. You watch each piece come out of the oil.
places.tip: Sit at the counter; lunch sets are the value play.

places.d: Two-star sushi counter. Pick it or Shoukouwa, not both.
places.tip: Book well ahead.

places.d: Hotel Cantonese, long starred: dim sum and double-boiled soups.
places.tip: Weekday dim sum lunch.

places.d: Ningbo seafood cooking: rare in Singapore, starred in 2026.
places.tip: For a group dinner with Chinese classmates.

places.addr: Flower Dome, Gardens by the Bay, 18 Marina Gardens Drive
places.d: Garden-inspired tasting menu inside the Flower Dome. Lovely setting; style risks outrunning substance.
places.tip: Lunch, with a dome visit attached.

places.addr: Gardens by the Bay, 18 Marina Gardens Drive
places.d: The steel tree-towers, free at ground level. The nightly light-and-sound show is genuinely worth it.
places.tip: Lie on the ground under the trees for the show (usually 7.45 and 8.45pm; check site).

places.addr: Gardens by the Bay, 18 Marina Gardens Drive
places.d: Two cooled glasshouses. The Cloud Forest's misted indoor mountain and waterfall is the better one.
places.tip: Late afternoon, then out for Supertrees at dusk.

places.d: Grass-roofed dam with skyline views: locals fly kites and picnic here at sunset.
places.tip: Bring a picnic and a bottle; walk on to the Supertrees after.

places.d: Lotus-shaped building with rotating exhibitions; quality varies by show.
places.tip: Only if the current show interests her.

places.d: The spitting lion. A 30-second tick on the promenade loop.
places.tip: Pass it on the walk; don't detour.

places.d: Arts centre with frequent free outdoor concerts and a rooftop terrace over the bay.
places.tip: Check the free-events listing; Labyrinth is in the mall.

places.d: DNA-spiral footbridge, best lit at night on the bay loop.
places.tip: Walk it after dark.

places.addr: Rooftop, The Fullerton Bay Hotel, 80 Collyer Quay
places.src: World's 50 Best Discovery; Time Out SG
places.d: Rooftop pool bar facing MBS head-on, with DJs Wednesday-Sunday. You come for the view and the drinks are fine.
places.tip: Sunset; hours conflict across listings, so check.

places.src: Time Out SG (Mar 2026 menu); former Asia's 50 Best Bars entrant
places.d: Serious hotel bar with bay views and a 2026 'Modern Localism' menu plus its own house gin.
places.tip: Window seat for the bay.

places.src: Heritage hawker market; Broadsheet / Makansutra canon
places.d: Victorian cast-iron market turned food court. Stalls inside are average-to-good; the satay street outside is the reason to come.
places.tip: From about 7pm Boon Tat St closes to cars: order satay at Best Satay 7 & 8 with a cold Tiger.

places.d: The old Golden Shoe hawkers (56 stalls) rehoused in a 2022 tower. A real CBD lunch with locals, not tourists.
places.tip: Before 12 or after 1.45pm on weekdays; closed or quiet on weekends for many stalls.

places.n: Ya Kun Kaya Toast (Far East Square)
places.d: The flagship of the kaya-toast chain: kopi, soft-boiled eggs, butter-and-kaya toast. A chain, but the original one.
places.tip: Kaya toast set with kopi C, 8am.

places.d: Honest North Indian on a busy terrace. The weekday lunch is the bargain Michelin flags.
places.tip: Mutton dum biryani; lunch.

places.d: Ex-Zén chef Nicolas Tam's pan-Asian tasting menu in a calm, organic-textured room with counter seats. Precise but playful, and fully her register.
places.tip: Ask for the counter. Amadai is his signature (Michelin).

places.src: Former Asia's 50 Best Bars No. 4 / World's 50 Best No. 10; Punch; FACT Awards nominee
places.d: The original unmarked-door speakeasy that put Singapore on the bar map. Still one of the better quiet drinks in town.
places.tip: Book; closed Sunday.

places.src: Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026 No. 16; Tatler Best 20 Bars 2026
places.d: Music-and-drinks hub with Asian-leaning playlists and playful classics. Closest thing to Caia in this patch.
places.tip: Later in the evening for the music.

places.d: Japanese craft cocktails and small plates in a heritage building, reached by a fire-escape staircase. From the Jigger & Pony group.
places.tip: Go hungry; the snacks are part of it.

places.addr: Boat Quay, along the Singapore River
places.d: Pretty restored shophouse frontage best seen from Cavenagh Bridge. The riverside restaurants are tourist traps with touts.
places.tip: Walk it, don't eat it.

places.d: Busan-born Sun Kim's Korean-modern single menu, mostly seafood and vegetables, with a Korean non-alcoholic pairing. Bold flavours, minimalist plating. Her best splurge on the river.
places.tip: Steamed Jeju abalone with gochujang seaweed risotto is the signature. Check opening days when booking.

places.d: Alsatian Christophe Lerouy's omakase-style French facing an open kitchen. Chef's-table energy, odd and clever flavour pairings.
places.tip: You pick the number of courses; small bar for a drink before. Closed Sun-Mon.

places.d: Vegetable-led French cooking from peak-season Savoie produce, in a white warehouse room above a print gallery. The most River Cafe-minded kitchen in this patch, with a great cheese trolley.
places.tip: Lunch Wed-Sat; finish on the cheese trolley and digestifs.

places.d: Rishi Naleendra's Sri Lankan, now at New Bahru. Michelin says the crab is the reason to come. One reviewer finds it toned down since the move, but it is still the best Bib on the river.
places.tip: Crab curry with hoppers. A la carte keeps it mid-price (set menu reported S$155).

places.src: Michelin Bib Gourmand 2026 (Beach Rd branch); Broadsheet, Sep 2026
places.d: The city's most-praised nasi lemak: obsessive coconut rice, sambal and fried chicken. This is the newer branch; the Bib is for Beach Rd.
places.tip: Nasi lemak + ayam goreng berempah; lunch.

places.src: Chope listing; SilverKris on Bjorn Shen (no 2026 critic review found)
places.d: Bjorn Shen's cult Middle Eastern Artichoke switched in late 2025 to a new-school pizza parlour. The talent is still there, but it's not the old mezze menu.
places.tip: Medium confidence on current menu; check before going.

places.n: Song Fa Bak Kut Teh (New Bridge Rd)
places.addr: 11 New Bridge Road, opposite Clarke Quay Central
places.d: Teochew peppery pork-rib soup with endless refills, at the original shop. Touristy queue but genuinely good.
places.tip: Go 10.30am or 3pm to dodge the line; add you tiao to dunk.

places.d: Proper neighbourhood hawker centre by the river with two Bib stalls. A ten-minute ride from home.
places.tip: No.18 Zion Road Fried Kway Teow and Zhi Wei Xian Zion Road Big Prawn Noodle; evening.

places.src: Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026 No. 90 (new entry); Tatler Best 20 Bars 2026
places.d: Living-room bar with vinyl, DJ nights and fermentation-driven cocktails, spun off from Le Bon Funk. Her Caia, five minutes from the river.
places.tip: Book; DJ nights; lamb skewer and the baloney sandwich.

places.d: Converted 1940s school turned creative cluster: 60-plus brands, design shops, cafés, Kotuwa and Bar Bon Funk.
places.tip: Make it an evening: shop, eat at Kotuwa, then upstairs to Bar Bon Funk.

places.d: Contemporary print and paper gallery in a riverside warehouse, usually free and usually empty.
places.tip: Before lunch at JAG upstairs.

places.d: The painted bridge and the shaded riverside path: Singapore's nicest flat walk or run, and close to home.
places.tip: Run it at 7am or walk it at dusk.

places.d: The specialty roaster that defined Singapore brunch. Busy weekend Aussie-style plates.
places.tip: Weekday morning; flat white.

places.d: Riverside coffee with outdoor tables. Fine, reliable, not special.
places.tip: Coffee before a river walk.

places.d: Classical French with a legendary wine list. More formal and old-school than Odette.
places.tip: Only if Odette is booked or for a wine-led night; lunch is the gentler price.

places.d: Contemporary Italian in a refurbished colonial house, with a strong Italian and natural wine list. Her best Italian bet in this patch.
places.tip: Hand-made tagliatelle with white truffle when in season (Oct-Dec).

places.addr: #02-01 House of Tan Yeok Nee, 101 Penang Road, 238466
places.src: Michelin 1 star 2026 (new) + Young Chef Award (Shusuke Kubota); Time Out SG
places.d: French-Japanese tasting menu in a restored 1885 Teochew mansion. New, ambitious, and the room alone is worth seeing.

places.d: Starred Teochew in a mall: cold crab, braised goose, oyster omelette done properly.

places.d: Chen Kentaro's Japanese-Sichuan. Mapo tofu and dan dan are the point.
places.tip: Lunch sets.

places.d: The pioneer of Singapore fine dining, still starred. Hotel setting.
places.tip: Wine-led dinner.

places.d: Hotel Cantonese, refined dim sum.
places.tip: Weekend dim sum, then Manhattan bar is upstairs.

places.addr: Singapore Marriott Tang Plaza, 320 Orchard Road
places.d: Ginza-pedigree sushi counter.
places.tip: Lunch counter.

places.d: Tomoo Kimura's aged-fish sushi counter, newly starred.
places.tip: Book ahead.

places.d: 16-seat pine counter: Osaka chef, French technique, seasonal Japanese produce, 6 or 8 courses.
places.tip: Counter only; reserve.

places.src: Michelin Bib Gourmand 2026 (listed as Indocafé, Newton)
places.d: Peranakan in a dark-wood colonial bungalow. Careful spice work, and it feels like a proper night out.
places.tip: Wagyu cheek rendang; laksa.

places.d: Old-school Indonesian; reviews in 2026 are split.
places.tip: Beef rendang; a mall lunch, not a destination.

places.d: The famous S$30-plus hotel chicken rice. A Singapore rite, but hawker chicken rice is better and a fifth of the price.

places.d: Adults-only Kyoto obanzai izakaya with a menu that changes daily. A favourite of Japanese expats in a scruffy mall full of them.
places.tip: Must order a drink; Tue-Sat from 6.30pm. Status last confirmed 2024.

places.src: Michelin Bib Gourmand 2026 (Alliance Seafood, Heng, Hup Kee, Kwang Kee, Song Kee)
places.d: The Crazy Rich Asians hawker centre. Touty and pricier than elsewhere, but five Bib stalls.
places.tip: Alliance Seafood sambal stingray; Hup Kee oyster omelette (new Bib 2026); Heng carrot cake. Agree prices first.

places.n: Da Shi Jia Big Prawn Mee
places.d: Rich prawn-head broth noodles with big prawns at the River Valley end of Orchard.
places.tip: Big prawn mee, dry with soup on the side.

places.src: Institution (est. 1919); no recent critic review found
places.d: Old Hainanese coffee shop for kaya toast and kopi.
places.tip: Breakfast before Da Shi Jia at lunch.

places.addr: Level 2, Conrad Singapore Orchard, 1 Cuscaden Road
places.src: Tatler Best 20 Bars 2026 (off Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026)
places.d: Glam New York-style hotel bar with barrel-aged cocktails and a famous Sunday brunch. Off the 50 Best list now but still polished.
places.tip: Weeknight Martini; the Sunday brunch is the indulgence.

places.addr: Lobby, Tower Wing, Shangri-La, 22 Orange Grove Road
places.src: Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026 No. 43; Tatler Best 20 Bars 2026
places.d: Blue-and-gold hotel bar with storytelling menus, ranked in 2026.
places.tip: After the Botanic Gardens at dusk.

places.d: Peanut-shells shophouse bar in a Peranakan terrace. Pure nostalgia, cheap-ish beer.
places.tip: Happy hour, then walk up Emerald Hill.

places.d: The single best thing in this patch: rainforest, lakes, swans and the orchid garden. Free, open early to late.

places.addr: Emerald Hill Road, off Orchard Road
places.d: A quiet lane of ornate 1900s Peranakan terraces 30 seconds off the mall strip.
places.tip: Dusk, walking uphill from Peranakan Place.

places.addr: #04-20/21 Takashimaya, Ngee Ann City, 391 Orchard Road
places.d: Southeast Asia's great bookshop flagship: huge, with strong Asian-literature and design sections.
places.tip: Rainy afternoon.

places.d: Showcase for local designers. A hit-and-miss but genuine alternative to the global flagships.
places.tip: Gifts to take home in December.

places.d: Unglamorous block stuffed with Japanese izakayas and karaoke: the Japanese expat after-work scene.
places.tip: Upper floors after 7pm.

walks.name: The river to the bay, from her doorstep
walks.best: Start ~4.30pm on a weekday to hit Gardens by the Bay at dusk for the 7.45pm Garden Rhapsody
stops: Song Fa Bak Kut Teh (New Bridge Rd)
walks.d: Pick up the river at Zion Rd (15 minutes on foot from Kampong Bahru via Havelock) and follow the shaded promenade downstream. Coffee detour up Martin Rd to Common Man, back down over the painted Alkaff Bridge, past STPI and the quiet Robertson Quay tables. Walk briskly through Clarke Quay's neon (Song Fa is across New Bridge Rd if hungry). Cross to Boat Quay, look back from Cavenagh Bridge by the Asian Civilisations Museum, round the Fullerton to the Merlion. Take the promenade past the Esplanade and over the lit Helix Bridge, then cut through Bayfront to the Supertrees for the light show. End with drinks at Lantern or MO Bar, or a taxi home in 10 minutes.
